name: United States
summary: By far the world's largest stock market: listed US companies were worth almost $69 trillion at the end of 2025. Shares trade mainly on the NYSE and Nasdaq. The S&P 500 is the benchmark most investors follow, and US trades already settle the next business day (T+1).

currency.name: US dollar
currency.note: For a euro investor, US shares carry currency risk: a stronger euro reduces the euro value of dollar holdings, a weaker euro increases it (Category L).

source.title: FTSE Equity Country Classification Process, v3.5, October 2026, Appendix 3 (FTSE Russell, PDF)

exchanges.name: New York Stock Exchange (NYSE)
exchanges.founded: 1792 (Buttonwood Agreement, signed by 24 stockbrokers on 17 May)
exchanges.hours: Core session 09:30–16:00 New York time, with opening and closing auctions. NYSE Arca also offers early (04:00–09:30) and late (16:00–20:00) sessions; other venues and brokers use different extended hours.
exchanges.note: Nasdaq publishes the same 2026 holidays and early closes.

exchanges.name: Nasdaq
exchanges.hours: Regular market 09:30–16:00 New York time; pre-market 04:00–09:30 and after-hours 16:00–20:00.

indexes.name: S&P 500
indexes.description: 500 leading US companies, covering about 80% of available market capitalisation. Calculated by S&P Dow Jones Indices.

indexes.name: Dow Jones Industrial Average (the Dow)
indexes.description: A price-weighted index of 30 prominent US companies: shares with higher prices have more weight (Category H).

source.title: Dow Jones Industrial Average (S&P Dow Jones Indices)

indexes.name: Nasdaq-100
indexes.description: Large companies listed on Nasdaq, excluding financial companies, so technology and other growth industries dominate.

regulators.name: Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC)
regulators.role: Federal regulator of the securities markets, public company disclosure, exchanges and brokers.

regulators.name: FINRA
regulators.role: Self-regulatory organisation for member broker-dealers, supervising them under SEC oversight; it also runs BrokerCheck, where you can look up a broker's registration.

investorProtection.name: SIPC
investorProtection.text: If a member brokerage firm fails, SIPC protects customers' securities and cash up to $500,000, including $250,000 for cash. It does not cover market losses.

investorProtection.name: FDIC deposit insurance
investorProtection.text: Bank deposits are insured to at least $250,000 at each FDIC-insured bank.

settlement.csd: The Depository Trust Company (DTC), part of DTCC
settlement.note: The SEC adopted the change from T+2 to T+1 on 15 February 2023.

source.title: New "T+1" Settlement Cycle: What Investors Need To Know (Investor.gov, U.S. SEC)

rules.title: Market-wide circuit breakers
rules.text: Trading across all US exchanges can be halted if the S&P 500 falls 7% (Level 1), 13% (Level 2) or 20% (Level 3) in a day (Category D).

source.title: Stock market circuit breakers (Investor.gov, U.S. SEC)

rules.title: Extended trading hours
rules.text: Many US venues and brokers offer trading before 09:30 and after 16:00 New York time, with lower liquidity and wider spreads (Category E).

taxes.glance: Non-residents: 30% US withholding on dividends, reduced under a tax treaty. Residents: long-term gains (assets held more than a year) taxed at 0%, 15% or 20% depending on income; short-term gains at ordinary income tax rates.

items.title: Dividends paid to foreign investors
items.text: US payers generally withhold 30% on dividends paid to non-resident aliens. A reduced rate may apply under a tax treaty between the investor's country and the United States.

items.title: For an Austrian investor
items.text: An Austrian bank can credit foreign withholding tax only up to 15% of the dividend (Category Q). Ask your bank how it applies the US treaty rate.

items.title: Capital gains (US residents)
items.text: Assets held more than one year produce long-term gains, taxed at 0%, 15% or 20% depending on taxable income; assets held one year or less produce short-term gains, taxed as ordinary income.

sources.title: Topic no. 409, Capital gains and losses (IRS)

access: Most Austrian banks and brokers offer trading in US shares, usually with currency conversion into dollars.
Some US shares are also traded on European venues in euros (Category D).
Indirectly, through funds or ETFs on the S&P 500 or other US indexes (Category H).

history.text: 24 stockbrokers sign the Buttonwood Agreement on 17 May, the official founding of the NYSE.
The stock market crash starts the Great Depression era (Category K).
Black Monday, 19 October: the largest one-day percentage fall in the Dow's history (Category K).
The US moves to T+1 settlement on 28 May.
Alphabet is announced as a new member of the Dow Jones Industrial Average (June).

funFacts: The NYSE traces its roots to a financial panic: the Buttonwood Agreement of 1792 was a response to the young nation's first financial panic.
US listed companies were worth about 224% of US GDP at the end of 2025 (World Bank/WFE).

sources.title: Alphabet set to join the Dow Jones Industrial Average, 23 June 2026 (S&P Dow Jones Indices)
